text:
maya: Heads-up — merged PR #8429 (kernel selector tweak) a few mins ago. Post-merge microbench smoke shows a small regression on the quant path for 2k seq (~+6% p95). bench artifact: https://ci.redwood/bench/1723456789 :eyes:
deploy-bot: Canary started for sha abc123 -> svc/runtime-canary (region: us-west2). canary tags: quant-v2
sam: Ugh, saw that. Can you paste the bench diff summary?
maya: Quick paste from bench run:
```
microbench/2kseq/quant-v1 -> p95=182ms, throughput=320 tps
microbench/2kseq/quant-v2 -> p95=194ms (+6.6%), throughput=305 tps (-4.7%)
alloc mem ~ +30MB per shard on average
```
maya: Link to perf heatmap + artifacts: https://ci.redwood/artifacts/1723456789/heatmap.html
alex: @maya thanks. Is this visible on canary logs or only bench harness?
maya: Mostly harness so far; canary traces haven't shown errors but tail latency ticked up a bit in 1/10 canary nodes (p95 -> ~210ms). Nothing fatal.
jin: Can we pin canary to quant-v1 or do a quick rollback while we triage?
sam: If it's only +6% p95 and mem +30MB, might be OK for a short period, but need eyes. @alex @jin can one of you take a quick look at the kernel selector diff? It's small but might change kernel launch params.
alex: I'll take a look in ~30m. If it's kernel launch config we can probably tweak the grid size back.
maya: TL;DR of change: prefer fused-kernel when seq_len > 512 to reduce thread divergence; maybe mis-classifying in a corner. Patch here: https://review.redwood/pr/8429
sam: Adding perf regression label and flagging for postmerge hold until we confirm root cause. If someone can confirm low-risk tweak to restore previous behavior, we can hotfix.
jin: Quick thought — could be related to the new prefetch order interacting with quant packer. I'll try reproducing locally on a small canary with the same seed.
maya: Thanks. If we do roll back/patch, request: keep canary up but route <20% traffic to it. Deploy-bot: can you set canary traffic to 10%?
deploy-bot: Command received: set canary traffic -> 10% (applied).
alex: Found one suspicious line in selector where we compare bytes_per_thread rounded down — might underutilize warp for certain seqs. I'll PR a revert to that line if tests pass.
sam: Great — ping here when you have a short revert PR. If not by EOD, we should consider rolling back fully.
maya: Appreciate the quick triage. Will monitor the bench and canary traces and post updates. :thumbsup:
